_doc: The jStack structure manifest — the CLOSED list of what this repo ships,
at its two roots: the repo top and the plugin top. Counted from git-tracked
entries (what a clone gets); untracked files are a session's work-in-progress
and out of scope, the same split manifest.sh draws. Enforcement is
tests/structure.sh, which the pre-push gate's layer 2 and the nightly
consumer checks already run — a stray folder cannot be pushed. Adding an
entry = adding it here, in the same commit, with a reason that survives
being read aloud.
THE BOUNDARY LAW. The plugin (plugins/jstack/) is mechanisms that run on a
machine that is not ours: parameterized only by userConfig (agent_root,
repo_root, agent_registry, ...) and JSTACK_* env overrides, never reading
outside itself, never assuming this host. The repo above it is distribution
and products: the marketplace catalogs, the installer, the companion app,
the host package. Anything that wants into plugins/jstack/ must pass the
works-on-a-stranger's-machine test; anything host-specific lives in that
host's own repo on top of the plugin, never inside it.
Name collisions, disambiguated once: plugins/jstack/systems.json is the
PLUGIN's registry — a host federates it into its own systems registry via
an _imports entry and edits it only here. plugins/jstack/docs/ documents
plugin systems. A host's config/systems.json and ~/Systems/ shelf are that
host's instances — same names, different owners; wire against the one whose
repo you are standing in.

repo_root..agents: codex-side marketplace pointer — the agents engine's catalog of this repo's plugins
repo_root..claude-plugin: Claude Code marketplace catalog — marketplace.json names the plugins this repo offers
repo_root..gitignore: keeps runtime state, credentials and Finder litter out of the public checkout
repo_root.README.md: the repo's front page; manifest.sh audits the counts it claims
repo_root.app: the jStack companion app — a product riding in the tooling repo; first candidate to split out if outside users ever install
repo_root.host: the host-side python package (jstack_host) — machine-local pieces a portable plugin cannot ship
repo_root.install.sh: the installer — directory-source marketplace, so git pull is the update
repo_root.release.sh: coordinated release build and evidence-gated promotion entry point
repo_root.plugins: the catalog's contents; today one plugin, jstack
repo_root.product.md: what jStack is as a product

plugin_root..claude-plugin: Claude Code plugin manifest — the version lives here
plugin_root..codex-plugin: codex plugin manifest — same version, bumped together (manifest.sh enforces parity)
plugin_root.bin: the shipped adapters — log_event, msg, seat, session-files and the rest
plugin_root.commands-stage: bare slash commands staged for a host's ~/.claude/commands
plugin_root.githooks: versioned git hooks for this checkout — .git/hooks symlinks resolve here
plugin_root.hooks: the Claude Code hook scripts — SessionStart, Stop, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse
plugin_root.prompts: model-bound text the hooks inject — file-sourced per the prompt-sourcing rule, loaded by hooks/_prompts.py
plugin_root.repo_seat.py: repo→seat resolution shared by the hooks and bin adapters
plugin_root.root.py: the one declaration an install derives its tree from
plugin_root.rules-stage: portable rules staged for symlink into a host's ~/.claude/rules
plugin_root.scheduler: the scheduler daemon and its install plumbing
plugin_root.skills: the skills — one directory per skill carrying SKILL.md
plugin_root.systems.json: the plugin's systems registry — federated into host registries
plugin_root.tests: the hermetic suite — every executable *.sh here runs on push (pre-push layer 2)
plugin_root.session_runtime.py: provider-neutral transcript facts and native Codex offline fork API
